title: Privacy policy
excerpt: What this site collects, what it deliberately does not, how long anything is kept, and how to have it removed.
content:
This policy explains what Onim does with data. It covers the calculator pages, the file tools, the blog, the reviews and likes, and the contact form. It is written to be read in one sitting, and it describes the site as it actually runs rather than a template of what a site might do.

In one paragraph: we do not have accounts, we do not store what you type into a calculator, files you open in a tool never leave your browser, and the only things we keep are the ones you deliberately send us — a contact message, a review, a like — plus ordinary web-server log lines. We do not sell data, we do not build advertising profiles, and we do not run third-party tracking scripts.

Who is responsible

Onim is a free tool library published and operated by the small independent team described on the About page. That team is the data controller for the small amount of personal data described here. The address for every data question — access, correction, deletion, objection — is the contact form, and messages sent through it reach the people who can act on them.

If a request concerns a message you sent us, a review you posted or a like you registered, say so in the subject line; it is routed to the same inbox either way, but the label saves a round trip.

What this site does not collect

It is easier to start with the absences, because they are the part that matters most:

  • No accounts. There is no sign-up, no login and no profile for visitors. The public site has no session cookie and no user table.
  • No storage of calculator inputs. The values you type into a calculator are used to compute the result in front of you. They are held in the page while you are on it and they are gone when you leave or reload. They are not written to a database and they are not attached to you.
  • No uploads. The file tools read the file you choose with the browser's own file APIs and process it inside the page. The file is never posted to a server; there is no upload endpoint for it to reach.
  • No advertising profiles. We do not run third-party tracking pixels, we do not build behavioural segments, and we do not pass anything you do here to a data broker.
  • No cross-site tracking. Nothing on Onim follows you to another website, and nothing from another website is used to recognise you here.

What we do collect, and why

Server logs

Like every web server, ours records each request: the IP address that made it, the date and time, the URL requested, the HTTP status and the browser's user-agent string. These lines exist to keep the site running — diagnosing errors, measuring load and spotting abuse — and they are kept for a short period (normally no more than thirty days) before being rotated out. They are not combined with anything else to identify a person, and they are not used for marketing.

Page counters

To know which pages are worth improving, the site keeps a daily counter per page: the page path, the date, and a number. There is no visitor identifier in that counter, no cookie, and no way to work backwards from it to a person. It answers "was this page read this week?", not "who read it".

The contact form

When you send a message we store the name, email address, phone number (if you fill it in), subject and message you submit, together with the IP address the message came from and the time it arrived. The IP address is used for one thing: rate limiting. A visitor can send five messages an hour, after which the form asks them to wait; that rule is what keeps the form usable for everyone else.

The message is stored in the site's database first and a notification email is sent to the team second, so a mail failure never loses your message. Messages are kept until the question is settled and for a short period afterwards in case of a follow-up, then deleted. Nothing in a contact message is ever used for marketing, added to a mailing list or shared with a third party.

Reviews and likes

Calculator pages let readers leave a review and register a like. A review stores the display name you choose, an optional title, the text of the review, the rating, the time it was posted and a shortened browser user-agent string — the last two so that spam and duplicate submissions can be recognised. Reviews are public: whatever you type in the name and text fields will be visible to anyone who opens the page. We do not ask for an email address on a review, and we do not publish the IP address or the cookie token with it.

A like stores only a count against the page. To stop one browser from voting repeatedly, the site keeps a small anonymous token (see Cookies) and a list of pages that token has already liked. That list is what "you have already liked this calculator" is read from. It contains no name, no email address and no browsing history outside this site.

Messages sent to the team about the site itself

If you email the team directly rather than using the form — for example about licensing, a legal request or a press enquiry — your message sits in that mailbox. It is kept for as long as the correspondence needs, and deleted when it no longer does.

Files you open in a tool

The Audio, Video, Image, PDF, Developer, Converter, Security, Compressor, Productivity and Text tools all run in the browser. The file you select is read into the page's memory, processed there, and offered back to you as a download. It is not transmitted, not cached on the server and not retained after you close or reload the tab. If a tool cannot do a job without sending the file somewhere, the page says so before you start, and no shipped tool currently needs to.

Cookies and local storage

The public site sets one cookie, and only when you use a feature that needs it: an anonymous token that remembers which pages you have already liked. It carries no personal information, and clearing it merely resets those counters. There are no advertising or analytics cookies on the site as shipped. The full list, with names and lifetimes, is on the cookie policy.

Analytics

As shipped, Onim runs no analytics script at all: page counts come from the server's own counter. If the operator of a deployment turns on a third-party analytics provider — Google Analytics 4, Plausible or Umami, chosen in the admin panel — then that provider's script loads on every page and its own privacy terms apply. This site's configuration is visible on the cookie policy page, which states which provider, if any, is active.

Advertising

The site is free because it is funded by advertising, but advertising here is deliberately small: a handful of clearly marked placements, never inside a result and never between you and an answer. We do not put your calculator inputs, your files or your reviews into an ad request. Where a placement is filled by a third-party network that uses cookies for frequency capping or measurement, that network's own policy governs its cookies, and the cookie policy lists the categories. On the deployment as shipped, no network script is loaded.

Who else sees data

Only the providers needed to run the site see anything at all, and each sees the minimum:

  • The hosting provider serves the pages and therefore sees the same request information your browser sends to any website (IP address, URL, user-agent).
  • The outbound mail provider carries the notification email for a contact message, which contains the message you wrote.
  • An analytics provider, if one is switched on, receives page views under its own terms, as described above.

We do not sell personal data. We do not share it with advertisers, data brokers or marketing platforms, and we do not transfer it for anyone else's purposes.

How long things are kept

Retention at a glance
WhatHow long
Server log linesA short period, normally no more than 30 days
Daily page countersIndefinitely, as aggregate numbers only
Contact messagesUntil the question is settled, plus a short follow-up window; deleted on request
ReviewsUntil you ask for removal, or until the page they belong to is retired
Like tokens and like listsUp to 12 months, or until the cookie is cleared
Calculator inputsNot stored at all
Files opened in a toolNot transmitted; gone when the tab closes

Your rights, and how to use them

If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland or another jurisdiction with a comparable framework, you have the right to ask for a copy of the personal data we hold about you, to have it corrected, to have it deleted, to restrict or object to its processing, and to receive it in a portable format. If you are in California, you have the right to know what is collected, to delete it, to correct it, and not to be discriminated against for exercising those rights.

In practice, the list above is short and concrete: contact messages, reviews and like tokens. Write through the contact form and say what you want — a copy, a correction, a deletion or an objection — and it will be handled by a person. We answer within 30 days and usually much sooner. There is a worked-out description of each route on the your data and your choices page.

Where processing needs a legal basis: server logs and abuse prevention rest on the legitimate interest of keeping the service available and safe; a contact message is handled because you asked us to answer it; a review or a like is published because you chose to post it. Nothing here depends on consent obtained through a pre-ticked box, because there is no such box.

Children

Onim is a general-purpose tool library, not a service aimed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 13, and the site asks for no personal details to use a calculator or a file tool. If a message or review appears to come from a child under 13, it is removed on request from a parent or guardian.

Security

The public pages are served over HTTPS. The admin area — which is not part of the public site and holds no visitor data beyond what is described above — requires a login and a session cookie. Form submissions carry a per-visitor token to prevent cross-site request forgery, and contact messages are rate-limited by IP. No system is perfect; if you find a problem, tell us through the contact form and it will be treated as urgent.

International transfers and hosting

The site is served from a hosting provider's data centre, which may be outside your country. That is inherent in visiting any website: the request has to travel to wherever the server is. We do not add any further transfer of your data between countries.

Changes to this policy

When something here changes, the date at the top of the page changes with it, and the change is described rather than silently made. Material changes — a new data category, a new provider, a different retention period — are noted in the section they affect. The policy has been written to match the code: if you find a sentence here that the site does not do, that is a bug, and we would like to hear about it.

Related pages

Cookie policy — every cookie and storage key, with names and lifetimes. Your data and your choices — how to request a copy or a deletion, step by step. AI policy — how AI tooling is and is not used on this site. Terms of use and Disclaimer — the rules of use and the limits of the results.
